title: They Looked Perfect Together… Until the Fruit Was Missing
paragraphs:
They Looked Perfect Together… Until the Fruit Was Missing
Why the Fruit of the Spirit Matters More Than Chemistry in Dating—and How Jesus Rewrites Even Our Worst Relationship Mistakes
It didn’t fall apart in one moment. It decayed quietly.

No explosion. No dramatic betrayal at first. Just small fractures—impatience in conversations, subtle manipulation dressed as “care,” jealousy disguised as passion, silence where truth should have lived.
And the terrifying part?
Everyone around them said they were “perfect together.”
But heaven wasn’t measuring perfection.
Heaven was measuring fruit.
Because attraction can lie. Chemistry can deceive. But fruit… fruit always tells the truth.
The Apostle Paul didn’t leave us guessing. In Galatians 5:22–23, he wrote something that cuts deeper the longer you stare at it:
“But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control.”
In the original Greek, it reads:

“Ὁ δὲ καρπὸς τοῦ Πνεύματος ἐστίν· ἀγάπη (agapē), χαρά (chara), εἰρήνη (eirēnē), μακροθυμία (makrothymia), χρηστότης (chrēstotēs), ἀγαθωσύνη (agathōsynē), πίστις (pistis), πραΰτης (prautēs), ἐγκράτεια (enkrateia).”
Not fruits. Fruit.
Singular.
Because it’s one life. One Spirit. One evidence.
And here’s what most people miss in dating: you don’t test compatibility by how good it feels in the moment—you test it by what kind of fruit grows over time.
You can hold hands in church and still lack agapē.
You can pray together and still lack makrothymia—that deep, long-suffering patience that refuses to quit when things get uncomfortable.
You can say “I love you” and still not have prautēs—gentleness that refuses to wound the other person with words, tone, or control.
And if we’re honest… some relationships don’t fail because the devil attacked them.
They fail because the Spirit was never leading them.
Jesus never said, “You will know them by their attraction.”
He said in Matthew 7:16:
“You will know them by their fruits.”
The Greek is piercing:
“ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς” (apo tōn karpōn autōn epignōsesthe autous)
You will recognise them fully by their fruit.
Not by their words. Not by their promises. Not by their potential.
By their fruit.
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable…
Some of us stayed in relationships because we were addicted to potential instead of anchored in truth.
We kept saying, “They’ll change.”
But the fruit kept saying, “They’re not led.”
And deep down, you knew.
You felt it when conversations turned cold instead of peaceful.
You noticed it when arguments became battles instead of opportunities for gentleness.
You sensed it when love felt conditional instead of sacrificial.
Because real, Spirit-led love looks like Christ.
And Christ never loved halfway.
In 1 Corinthians 13:4–7, Paul describes love again, and the Greek strips away every romantic illusion:

“Ἡ ἀγάπη μακροθυμεῖ (makrothymei) — love suffers long
χρηστεύεται (chrēsteuetai) — is kind
οὐ ζηλοῖ (ou zēloi) — does not envy
οὐ περπερεύεται (ou perpereuetai) — does not boast
οὐ φυσιοῦται (ou physioūtai) — is not puffed up…”
This is not dating advice.
This is spiritual diagnosis.
Because if your relationship consistently produces anxiety instead of peace, control instead of gentleness, emotional chaos instead of self-control…
That’s not love growing.
That’s flesh operating.
Galatians 5:19–21 makes that brutally clear—the works of the flesh: jealousy, fits of anger, selfish ambition, dissensions.
Some of us called it “passion.”
God calls it evidence.
And yet… here’s where grace interrupts the story.
Because this isn’t just about exposing what’s broken.
It’s about redeeming what feels too far gone.
There was a woman in John 4 who had a history that would disqualify her in every modern dating conversation.
Five husbands.
And the man she was with wasn’t even hers.
Scandal.
Mess.
Complication.
And yet Jesus didn’t walk away.
He leaned in.
He spoke truth without crushing her.
He offered living water instead of condemnation.
In the Aramaic context, when Jesus speaks of “living water,” it carries the sense of life that flows continuously—not stagnant, not borrowed, but divine.
Because Jesus doesn’t just fix relationships.
He rewrites identities.
Which means your dating history doesn’t disqualify you.
Your mistakes don’t cancel your future.
Your past doesn’t get the final word.
Grace does.
But grace doesn’t ignore fruit.
It transforms it.

Because when the Holy Spirit truly leads your life, the fruit will show up not just in church, not just in prayer—but in how you love someone when they frustrate you, how you respond when they disappoint you, how you choose truth when it would be easier to manipulate.
Dating becomes discipleship.
Not performance. Not pretending. Not pressure.
But formation.
Two people becoming more like Christ—or pulling each other away from Him.
And that’s the question you can’t avoid:
Is this relationship producing the fruit of the Spirit… or just emotional attachment?
Be honest.
This hit deeper than you expected, didn’t it?
Because your honesty might be the beginning of someone else’s healing too.
And don’t keep this to yourself.
Someone you love is in a relationship right now that looks good on the outside but is starving on the inside.
And if you’ve been searching for deeper truth like this—real, Scripture-rooted, life-exposing, Christ-centred—then stay close.
Because this isn’t content.
This is transformation.
And if you feel God stirring something deeper in you… if you don’t just want inspiration but discipleship, accountability, growth, and daily spiritual nourishment… then take the next step.
Because supporting this mission isn’t about a transaction.
It’s about participation in the Gospel.
It’s about helping truth reach more hearts.
It’s about glorifying God through what you choose to stand behind.
And if this message stirred something in you… don’t ignore it.
That’s not emotion.
That’s invitation.
The kind that changes everything.
Because the most dangerous relationship isn’t the one that ends.
It’s the one that slowly pulls you away from Christ while convincing you it’s love.
And the most powerful one?
Is the one where both people are being transformed by Him.
